memories.content: Link expected participant burden in each user study task to its corresponding mitigation strategy.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the prototype and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided during user study sessions.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately after collection.
Specify the equipment to be loaned to participants who lack necessary devices.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
HCI ethics reviewers verify that expected burdens and mitigation strategies correspond to each user study task.
Inform participants that the formative evaluation prototype is not a finished service.
Set an upper limit on cumulative task burden when requesting repeated evaluations from the same participant.
The author of this proposal tends to emphasize expected benefits of the prototype over participant burden.
In organizations where leaders or institutional staff handle recruitment, recruitment authority and academic or professional evaluation authority may be combined in the same role.
List whom to notify and in what order if serious discomfort is reported during the study.
Field staff rely on the pre-defined contact sequence when serious discomfort is reported.
Define the thresholds for participant harm, operational disruption, and data anomalies at which deployment and data collection must cease.
Establish procedures to restore existing systems and workflow states after suspending field deployment.
The user's stop plan can be judged feasible only when it identifies who has authority to order recovery and who is responsible for carrying it out.

In organizations where error reporting is linked to individual performance evaluations, safety signal records may be separated from research decision logs, potentially breaking the traceability path for the same incident.

analysis.overview: The frames address complementary but independent ethics controls. The reference centers on participant access, burden, privacy, equipment, disclosure, reviewer practice, and recruitment power; the compared frame centers on discomfort escalation, deployment cessation and recovery, and incident traceability. Neither contains a scope-aligned counterpart to the other’s claims.

relations.reason: These memories describe specification and verification stages of one reference-only task-level burden-control claim; the compared frame has no operational counterpart.
relations.summary: Expected participant burdens and mitigations are mapped to individual study tasks and checked by ethics reviewers.

relations.reason: Both memories split the planning and provision of one reference-only accommodation claim; the compared frame does not address participant access.
relations.summary: Necessary accessibility accommodations are identified and their delivery during study sessions is specified.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only privacy control with no corresponding compared-side claim.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers are separated from research data immediately after collection.

relations.reason: The memories cover provision and return within one reference-only equipment-support process; the compared frame has no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: Necessary devices are loaned to participants who lack them, with a defined return procedure.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only participant disclosure with no compared-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Participants are told that the formative-evaluation prototype is not a finished service.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only safeguard for repeated participation, not addressed by the compared frame.
relations.summary: Repeated evaluations involving the same participant are subject to an upper cumulative task-burden limit.

relations.reason: This reference-only observation concerns framing bias and has no operationally corresponding compared-side claim.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to emphasize prototype benefits over participant burden.

relations.reason: This is a reference-only organizational power condition; the compared frame’s performance-linked reporting condition concerns a different decision and risk.
relations.summary: Institutional recruitment arrangements may combine recruitment authority with academic or professional evaluation authority in one role.

relations.reason: The memories state the definition and operational use of one compared-only escalation procedure; the reference frame has no corresponding incident-response claim.
relations.summary: A predefined notification sequence governs whom field staff contact, and in what order, after serious discomfort is reported.

relations.reason: These memories specify complementary parts of one compared-only suspension-and-recovery control; the reference frame does not govern deployment cessation or restoration.
relations.summary: A deployment stop plan defines cessation thresholds, restoration procedures, recovery-ordering authority, and execution responsibility.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only recordkeeping risk; the reference frame’s authority condition does not address incident-log traceability.
relations.summary: Performance-linked error reporting may separate safety-signal records from research decision logs and break incident traceability.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only material covers serious-discomfort escalation, harm and disruption stop thresholds, deployment recovery responsibilities, and incident-traceability risks created by performance-linked reporting.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only material covers task-level burden mitigation, accommodations, identifier separation, equipment support, prototype-status disclosure, cumulative burden, proposal bias, and combined recruitment and evaluation authority.
